## Sources (how this label entered the ledger)
- **OBJECT-INDEX** (batch B0033, scope OBJECT): Book chapter III.2 formally defines Goal G as Knower-owned intent that INDUCES knowledge requirements without containing, evaluating, or acting on them, discovered under adversarial falsification pressure to have exactly ONE direct consumer (the Proposal selector) -- everywhere else in the model 'the goal requires...' actually means EC. Formally defines IdealState as the standard of sufficiency the Knower holds, explicitly NOT a picture of an ideal world and NOT a target state of reality, retelling the corpus's 'best one-hour drama': introduced at 00:08 as a major clarification, broken at 00:17 by its own author's worked example (the first version let the ideal drift toward a world-description, which the example showed collapses into circularity and violates the complement principle), repaired the same night into the surviving reading -- explaining why the architecture resists ever 'learning' the IdealState from data ('a learned standard is an unowned standard'). Gives three contrast cases each showing the standard misplaced: 'a fully audited election' (wrong -- a world-state, not a knowledge standard), '99% confidence in the result' (wrong twice -- collapses a structured standard into a scalar and treats sufficiency as a number), 'whatever the audit software reports as complete' (wrong in the way that matters most -- hands the standard to a mechanism, and 'who set the bar?' must never answer 'the pipeline').
